The projective sublevel-radius transform R(z)=(1+z)r((z-1)/(z+1))/sqrt(2) gives the small-radius inverse with coefficient 1/[n(n+1)c_0^(n-1)]. At t=1 put q=-r'; q'/q^(n+2)->b^(n-1) with b=k_n^(1/n). Integrating and inverting gives the claimed large-radius exponent 1/(n+1), negative correction and stated coefficient. Direct algebra checks c_0*c_infinity=1. Convex radiality makes the limiting slope the global Lipschitz constant; if slopes were equal the profile would be affine, contradicting r'(1-)=-infinity. Conjugate zero ball is the origin subgradient and the open effective-domain ball follows from the negative unbounded sublinear correction on its boundary. These are analytic deductions, not inferred from the n=2..40 verifier.
